title: VPC Prepare Validator Suite for Private Deployments
creator: Maria Chen
description: Create a reusable, cloud-agnostic validator suite that runs before Private (VPC) installs. The suite must validate resource quotas, IAM roles and policies, DNS/private zone configuration, available GPU capacity (counts and types), network addressability, and common peripheral limits (ENIs, EBS) across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Output should be both machine-readable (JSON report) for CI and human-friendly for the operator UI. The validator will be integrated with the Terraform/IaC flow (as an opt-in pre-apply check and as a Github Action) and surface actionable remediation hints where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Validator runs as a standalone binary and as a Terraform external/null_resource step
Checks cover: cloud quotas (vCPU, GPUs, EBS), IAM role existence and required policies, private DNS forwarding/conditional zones, subnet / IP availability, ENI and security group limits
GPU capacity check returns counts by instance type and verifies CUDA/NVIDIA driver compatibility via node image hints
Validator emits a JSON report and exit code: 0 = pass, 1 = warnings, 2 = fatal failures
Integration test exists that simulates a failing quota and a failing DNS entry using mocked cloud APIs
GitHub Action created that runs validator on PRs touching private-deploy Terraform modules
Operator-facing remediation suggestions are populated for at least 70% of fatal failures (e.g., request quota increase link, example IAM policy snippet, Terraform module override)
technical_notes: Design: implement validator as a Go CLI that uses cloud SDKs with pluggable provider adapters (aws, gcp, azure). Keep logic provider-agnostic in core module.
Terraform hookup options: (A) terraform null_resource with local-exec to run validator before apply; (B) a custom provider is out-of-scope for MVP
Checks will use both declarative expectations (from terraform variables or a separate manifest) and live discovery (query quotas/capacity).
GPU check: query cloud's capacity APIs and cross-reference requested instance types; if exact counts unavailable, sample on recent spot/market data and warn
DNS check: validate private zone exists and that resolver rules/routes are present between VPCs; for AWS verify Route53 private hosted zone zone_id and VPC association
IAM check: verify IAM role ARNs exist, attached policies include required actions; for cross-account roles also validate trust policy principals
Idempotence: validator must be safe to run multiple times and not modify infrastructure (only read-only operations for IAM/quotas). Optional auto-remediation must be explicit and gated.
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement provider adapter interface, basic AWS quota and IAM checks (ENG-8672-1 branch)
Week 2: add GCP and Azure adapters, implement DNS and network range checks; wire Terraform null_resource pattern
Week 3: GPU capacity heuristics, machine-readable report format, and GitHub Action integration
Week 4: end-to-end integration tests, documentation, and add runbook entries to Console operator guide
Deliverables: CLI binary, terraform examples in modules/validator, github action workflow, integration tests + example failing PR screenshots
testing_plan: Unit tests for provider adapters (mock SDK clients)
Integration tests using recorded fixtures (VCR) against small dedicated test accounts
CI smoke: run validator in ephemeral AWS test account created by test harness to validate a scenario with insufficient GPU quota
Manual acceptance: run validator against customer-like staging VPC and confirm operator remediation text maps to actual Terraform fixes
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha — run on infra-eng PRs and optional pre-apply for internal private installs
Phase 2: enable GitHub Action template for customers using our private-deploy repo and document integration steps
Phase 3: bake validator output into Console preflight UI with link to remediation docs
Rollback: validator is read-only by default; revert GitHub Action and null_resource hooks if blocking pipeline unexpectedly
risk: Medium — incorrect false positives may block installs; permission scopes required for validator could be sensitive (needs least-privilege guidance).
